judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema strips refresh_token and all non-numeric fields from the token response, and the stripped result is then persisted back into Credential.key, silently destroying the stored refresh_token. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, Google (CalendarService.ts:94-99) and O365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts) pass their full credential object through parseRefreshTokenResponse; zod's default stripping reduces it to only access_token and any numeric field, then `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token'` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal placeholder string, and the caller writes this to prisma.credential.update. The original refresh_token is irrecoverably lost — the credential can never be refreshed again outside the sync endpoint, and any credential created before the sync endpoint was configured is permanently broken. This is silent, unrecoverable data loss in the Credential.key column with no rollback path.

adjudication.rationale: The claimed “silent data loss” via Zod stripping/persisting isn’t verifiable from the diff because `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is not a true catch-all schema: it uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which become a literal property name (e.g., "ZodString"), making the schema likely *fail* parsing for normal OAuth token objects rather than successfully strip fields. In that failure case, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws (`throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")`), so the update path that would overwrite/persist a placeholder refresh token is not shown to occur silently. While the new helper has serious issues, the specific mechanism and outcome described (successful parse → stripping → placeholder refresh_token persisted, irrecoverable silent loss) doesn’t match what can be confirmed from this diff alone.
